issues.title: The analyst session launched by `A` is given a front-matter contract that omits `attachments:` - it can drop the attachments the CLI just wrote
issues.description: FR4/FR5 make `attachments:` a real front-matter key that the `A` flow writes into the plan file and THEN launches a Claude session on that same file: `finishPlanWithClaude` calls `plans.SetAttachments(...)` (cli/internal/tui/plans_tab.go:1124) and immediately launches `AuthorPlanIntent` at `plans.Path(...)` with the instruction "read and edit ONLY that one file". That session runs `skills/gogo-project-plan/SKILL.md`, whose "Output contract (FR2 parses this - keep it exact)" block (skills/gogo-project-plan/SKILL.md:59-91) shows the plan file's front matter as literally `id / title / status / targets` and protects exactly one key by name ("Keep the front-matter correlation id. Do not remove or change the `id:` line."). Nothing tells the analyst that `attachments:` exists or must be preserved, so an LLM rewriting the front matter to match the shown template silently drops it. Per D3=A the path IS the only record (attachments are referenced, never copied), so the loss is unrecoverable, and it lands on the exact flow FR5 was built for. This is code-review-standards check #1 (every enumeration that changed must be in sync in EVERY place that enumerates it) - the plan's FR6 doc-sweep list simply did not include this skill.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. In `skills/gogo-project-plan/SKILL.md`: (a) add `attachments: /abs/mockup.png, https://example.com/spec` to the Output-contract front-matter block with a one-line note that the cockpit writes it at mint; (b) generalise the preservation rule from "keep the `id:` line" to "PRESERVE every front-matter key you did not author (`id:`, `created:`, `attachments:`, `members:`) - you own only `title:`, `status:` and `targets:`"; (c) add one line telling the analyst it may READ the listed attachments (a local path is a file on this machine, a URL is a link, never fetched by gogo itself). Also re-check `skills/gogo-plan/SKILL.md` for the same omission if a spawned work item ever rewrites a plan's front matter.
issues.fix_summary: skills/gogo-project-plan/SKILL.md: attachments: added to the output-contract front matter, preservation rule generalised to every cockpit-written key (id/created/attachments/members; analyst owns only title/status/targets), and a read-the-attachments line added. skills/gogo-plan/SKILL.md re-checked and updated per REV-003. VERIFIED round 2: SKILL.md:68 carries the key in the contract block; :90-94 is the generalised PRESERVE rule naming id/created/attachments/members and calling out that the path is the ONLY record; :95-97 is the READ line with the never-fetched caveat. gogo-plan re-checked - it writes only a source `.gogo/work/`, never a `~/.gogo/` plan file, so it has no front matter to preserve (grep: no plan-file write).

issues.title: `newForm()` is the single form construction site by convention only - nothing fails if a future `huh.NewForm(` re-appears
issues.description: D5=A chose the 12-site `newForm()` swap over the 2-site fix for exactly one reason: to stop the next `huh.NewText` field silently regressing to "enter submits" (plan.md, Approach 3: "coding-rules.md names enumeration-drift as this repo's top trap; a single construction site is the cheap structural answer"). The producer shipped (cli/internal/tui/model.go:149) and all 12 sites call it today, but the wiring is unpinned: a new form written as `huh.NewForm(huh.NewGroup(...))` compiles, passes `go vet`, and passes the whole suite - the exact failure shape code-review-standards #12 names ("pin the wirings, not just the producer - a call site can stop calling the producer and hand-write fresh copy with the whole suite green") and #11(a) ("add a test that fails if either site re-inlines it"). The repo already has both precedents for the cheap guard: `TestSkillsBashNoUnsafeRm` (source grep) and `TestPlansTabKeyHelpInSync` (AST walk of the package source).
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Add a package-source guard in `cli/internal/tui` (e.g. `TestNewFormIsTheOnlyFormConstructionSite`): walk/grep every non-test `*.go` in the package for the literal `huh.NewForm(` and fail unless the only occurrence is inside `newForm` in `model.go`, with an error message that names the offending file and says "use newForm(...) so gogoKeyMap's Text bindings apply". Mirror `switchKeys`'s AST approach in plans_view_test.go, or a plain source scan like TestSkillsBashNoUnsafeRm - either is ~15 lines.
issues.fix_summary: Added TestNewFormIsTheOnlyFormConstructionSite (source scan over the tui package): fails unless the ONLY huh.NewForm( occurrence is inside newForm() in model.go, naming the offending file and the newForm(...) remedy. VERIFIED round 2 by mutation, not by reading: in a scratch copy of cli/, rewriting move.go's `newForm(huh.NewGroup(` back to `huh.NewForm(huh.NewGroup(` compiles + vets clean and the guard FAILS with `move.go calls huh.NewForm( directly (1x) - use newForm(...)`. grep confirms exactly one huh.NewForm( in non-test source (model.go:150). Follow-up on the guard's reachability filed separately as REV-009 (does not reopen this).

issues.title: `WithAttachments` appends prose AFTER `--correlation` / `--skip-acceptance`, contradicting the gogo-plan skill's "always the FINAL token" contract
issues.description: `launch.WithAttachments` appends its clause to the end of `Intent.Command` (cli/internal/launch/launch.go:308). At the two `/gogo:plan` sites this runs after the params are already on the command: `planCreateWorkItem` (plans_tab.go:537, after `PlanIntent` appended `--correlation plan-XXXX`) and `finishPlanSpawn` (plans_tab.go:730, after `intent.Command += launch.SkipParams(...)`). The consumer states the opposite invariant: skills/gogo-plan/SKILL.md:42-45 - "The AUTHORITATIVE id is the LAST (trailing) `--correlation plan-XXXX` token: the cockpit CLI always appends it as the FINAL token of the invocation" - and :54-56 - "`--skip-acceptance` ... is a trailing literal, so a body that merely mentions the words is ordinary prose (never a flag)". After 0.30.0 that sentence is false for any plan with attachments. Verified impact today is limited (the clause contains no `--correlation`/`--skip-acceptance` lookalike, so "the LAST token" still resolves to the real one, and the stripped-goal remainder legitimately includes the attachments clause), so this is contract/doc drift rather than a live parse break - but it removes the disambiguation guarantee the skill leans on and leaves a producer and its consumer describing different command shapes.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE, either way: (a) preferred - update skills/gogo-plan/SKILL.md Step 0 to say the cockpit appends the params after the goal and MAY follow them with a trailing attachments clause, so the rule becomes "honor the LAST `--correlation plan-XXXX` / `--skip-acceptance` TOKEN anywhere in the invocation" rather than "the final token of the invocation", and note the clause is prose to be read as part of the brief; or (b) make the composition order match the stated contract by having `WithAttachments` insert the clause immediately after the goal (before the trailing params) at the two `/gogo:plan` sites. Whichever is chosen, keep the docs/cli-contract.md 0.30.0 note consistent with it.
issues.fix_summary: Option (a): skills/gogo-plan/SKILL.md Step 0 now says the authoritative id is the LAST --correlation token ANYWHERE in the invocation and that a trailing 0.30.0 attachments clause may follow the params (prose, read as part of the brief); the --skip-acceptance wording updated to match. docs/cli-contract.md note stays consistent (it never claimed token order). VERIFIED round 2: SKILL.md:42-48 + :58-59 now describe exactly the shipped composition order - planCreateWorkItem (PlanIntent's --correlation, then WithAttachments, then FoldToPointer) and finishPlanSpawn (SkipParams, then WithAttachments, then FoldToPointer). The fold still lands: FoldToPointer replaces in.Body inside in.Command, which the appended clause leaves intact, so the attachments clause survives an over-budget fold.

issues.title: The comma refusal (D4/FR4.4) checks the RAW line, but the STORED value is the absolutized path - a comma can re-enter via cwd or $HOME
issues.description: `normalizeAttachment` refuses a comma on the line the user typed (cli/internal/tui/plans_tab.go:859) and then returns a value the user never typed: `~`-expanded (line 869-873) and `filepath.Abs`-ed (line 874). A relative attachment typed inside a directory whose path contains a comma (or a `~` path under a home dir containing one) is accepted and stored as e.g. `attachments: /Users/me/a,b/shot.png`. `plans.render` joins on ", " (cli/internal/plans/plans.go:251) and `parseList` splits on "," (plans.go:~197), so the single attachment silently becomes two bogus entries on the next read - precisely the "silently corrupted" outcome D4=A was resolved to prevent ("rare; refused loudly, never silently corrupted"). Rare, but the check is one line away from being airtight and the store has no second line of defence.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Move (or duplicate) the comma refusal so it also runs on the NORMALIZED value: in `normalizeAttachment`, after computing `abs`, re-check `strings.Contains(abs, ",")` and return a named error ("the resolved path %q contains a comma, which the attachments: list cannot store - move the file or pass a comma-free path"). Optionally belt-and-braces the store too: have `plans.SetAttachments`/`AddAttachment` drop or reject comma-bearing entries rather than writing an unparseable line. Extend TestAttachmentNormalize with a `t.TempDir()`-based case whose directory name contains a comma.
issues.fix_summary: normalizeAttachment re-checks the comma on the NORMALIZED (abs) value with a named resolved-path error; TestAttachmentNormalize gains a comma-bearing-TempDir case driven via a relative path + Chdir. VERIFIED round 2: plans_tab.go re-checks strings.Contains(abs, ",") after filepath.Abs and BEFORE os.Stat, with the exact resolved-path message; both the $HOME (tilde-expansion) and cwd (relative-path) re-entry routes pass through that one check, and the URL branch returns earlier so the raw check still owns it. The new test case chdirs into a `a,b` TempDir and asserts the refusal names "comma" - it passes uncached under -race.

issues.title: The always-on project header row spends 2 more terminal rows than the plans kanban budgets for (`colAvail()` unchanged)
issues.description: FR2.2's header row is unconditional: `viewPlansBoard` now prepends the project line plus a blank line (cli/internal/tui/plans_tab.go:1258-1263) while `renderPlanColumn` still windows its cards against the SHARED `colAvail()` (cli/internal/tui/plans_tab.go:1297 -> cli/internal/tui/window.go:43-45). `colAvail`'s own doc comment defines the budget as "the whole height minus the board chrome (header, status, footer = 3 rows) and the column's own head + blank line (2 rows)" - so the plans tab's chrome grew from tabbar+blank+[status]+help to tabbar+blank+PROJECT+blank+[status]+help while the budget it computes against did not move. A full column therefore renders ~2 rows more than the viewport can show, and the rows that fall off the bottom are the status line and the help line - i.e. exactly the surfaces standards #8 ("rendered, not just set") and the 0.28.0 diagnosability bar rely on. No test measures the rendered height, so nothing catches it.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. Give the plans kanban its own budget rather than reusing the board's: add `planColAvail() int { return m.colAvail() - 2 }` (or `- planHeaderRows` with the constant used by both `viewPlansBoard` and the windowing) and use it in `renderPlanColumn` and `reflowPlanColumns`. Add a rendering test that sets a known `m.height`, fills a column past it, and asserts `lipgloss.Height(m.View()) <= m.height` with a status set - the guard the board never had.
issues.fix_summary: Added planColAvail() (colAvail - 1 for the tab's extra chrome, - 2 more for the project header row + blank) used by BOTH reflowPlanColumns and renderPlanColumn; TestPlansBoardFitsTerminalHeight pins lipgloss.Height(View()) <= m.height with a status set and the help line last. VERIFIED round 2, arithmetic and by mutation. Arithmetic: plans-tab chrome is tabbar+blank (view.go:33) + header+blank (viewPlansBoard) + status + help = 6, plus the column's own head+blank = 8, and planColAvail returns height-8 (height-6 when m.project is nil, matching the header-less render). grep confirms no plans path still calls colAvail(). Mutation: reverting planColAvail to `return m.colAvail()` in a scratch copy makes TestPlansBoardFitsTerminalHeight fail with "renders 25 rows into a 24-row terminal" - the guard bites.

issues.title: `plans.AddAttachment` ships exported with no caller and no test
issues.description: cli/internal/plans/plans.go:471 adds an exported `AddAttachment(project, id, att string) (Plan, error)`. `grep -rn AddAttachment cli/` finds only its own definition - no production call site, no test, and no CLI verb behind it (`gogo plan new --attach` is explicitly out of scope in plan.md). The plan's Changes checklist for `cli/internal/plans/plans.go` lists only `SetAttachments`; `AddAttachment` appears solely as a line in the class diagram. It is now also documented as shipped API in docs/cli-contract.md's 0.30.0 note. That is untested exported surface plus scope creep against coding-rules' "Keep diffs minimal and scoped to the plan".
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE - pick one and be consistent: (a) drop `AddAttachment` and remove it from docs/cli-contract.md's 0.30.0 note and from charts/class.mmd (smallest diff, matches the Changes checklist); or (b) keep it and give it the guard the sibling `AddTarget` has - a plans_test.go case covering append, the idempotent already-attached no-op, the blank-input no-op and the missing-plan error.
issues.fix_summary: Option (a): dropped plans.AddAttachment (no caller, not in the Changes checklist); removed from docs/cli-contract.md 0.30.0 note and charts/class.mmd (layouts regenerated). SetAttachments remains the one write path. VERIFIED round 2: `grep -rn AddAttachment` over *.go / *.md / *.mmd / *.json finds no live reference - gone from plans.go, from the cli-contract 0.30.0 note, from charts/class.mmd and from charts/layouts.json (regenerated, and it picked up the new attachmentsField / normalizeAttachment / focusChosenProject rows). SetAttachments keeps its round-trip / re-save / trim coverage in plans_test.go. The one straggler is the charts/manifest.json note, filed separately as REV-008 (it does not reopen this).

issues.title: An attachment that is a DIRECTORY is accepted, though the refusal message promises "an existing local file"
issues.description: `normalizeAttachment` validates a local path with a bare `os.Stat(abs)` (cli/internal/tui/plans_tab.go:878) and only rejects on error, so a directory (or any non-regular entry) passes while the message on the failure branch says "not an existing local file (nor an http(s):// URL)". The launched session is then told "a local path is a file on this machine" (cli/internal/launch/launch.go:283) and will fail to read it. Cosmetic-severity, but it makes a validation message untrue and pushes a knowable refusal into the launched session.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. In `normalizeAttachment`, capture the `os.FileInfo` and require `st.Mode().IsRegular()`, with a distinct message for the directory case (e.g. `%q: is a directory - attach a file`). Add the case to TestAttachmentNormalize using `t.TempDir()` itself as the input.
issues.fix_summary: normalizeAttachment now requires st.Mode().IsRegular() with a distinct 'is a directory - attach a file' error; TestAttachmentNormalize covers a directory input. VERIFIED round 2: the stat result is captured and `!st.Mode().IsRegular()` returns the distinct message, which also hedges correctly for a socket/fifo ("or not a regular file"); os.Stat follows symlinks so a symlink to a real file still passes. The test feeds t.TempDir() itself and asserts the error names "directory".

issues.title: The as-built `charts/manifest.json` note still advertises `plans.AddAttachment` that REV-006 deleted
issues.description: REV-006's fix removed `AddAttachment` from the code, from docs/cli-contract.md's 0.30.0 note, from charts/class.mmd and from charts/layouts.json - but not from the as-built manifest note that DESCRIBES those diagrams. `.gogo/work/feature-project-first-plan-authoring/charts/manifest.json:4` was rewritten this round to "As-built (phase 2)" and still reads "class = the structures the change added (plans.Plan.Attachments + SetAttachments/AddAttachment, ...)". So the manifest claims a shipped API that exists neither in `cli/internal/plans/plans.go` nor in the class diagram the same sentence is describing (verified: `grep -rn AddAttachment` finds it only here, in plan.md's plan-time class diagram, and in the review/implement audit records). This is code-review-standards #1 in miniature - the enumeration changed in one place and not in the place that enumerates it - and the manifest is the note that rides into the report bundle at phase 5, so the stale claim outlives this feature folder.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE. In `.gogo/work/feature-project-first-plan-authoring/charts/manifest.json`, drop `/AddAttachment` from the `note` so it reads `plans.Plan.Attachments + SetAttachments`. One token. (Leave `plan.md`'s class diagram alone - that is the accepted plan-time intent record, and phase 5 is what reconciles it to as-built.)
issues.fix_summary: charts/manifest.json note: 'SetAttachments/AddAttachment' -> 'SetAttachments' (matches the REV-006 deletion and the updated class diagram).

issues.title: `TestNewFormIsTheOnlyFormConstructionSite` passes VACUOUSLY if its directory scan finds nothing - and a sibling test in the same file mutates the process cwd it depends on
issues.description: The REV-002 guard scans `os.ReadDir(".")` and reports a violation only from inside the per-file loop (cli/internal/tui/plans_tab_test.go:1455-1476). With zero matching entries the loop never runs and the test PASSES green - test-strategy.md variant 6 ("an exclusivity/invariant assertion that is true VACUOUSLY ... pair it with a reachability guard"). It never asserts it actually saw `model.go`, nor that it scanned any file at all. The precedent REV-002 explicitly named, `TestSkillsBashNoUnsafeRm`, has exactly that guard and this one dropped it: `if len(skills) == 0 { t.Fatal("no skills/*/SKILL.md found - wrong cwd? (expected to run from cli/)") }` (cli/skills_lint_test.go:44-46). The dependency is not hypothetical: `TestAttachmentNormalize`, in the SAME FILE and running just before it, changes the process working directory with raw `os.Chdir` + a manual `t.Cleanup` restore (plans_tab_test.go:1333-1342) rather than Go 1.25's `t.Chdir` (go.mod says `go 1.25.0`), which restores as a framework guarantee. Verified by two-part mutation in a scratch copy of `cli/`: with the defect the guard exists to catch reintroduced (move.go calling `huh.NewForm(` directly) AND the manual restore dropped, `go vet` is clean and BOTH tests report PASS - the wiring guard silently stops guarding. It bites correctly today (same defect, cwd intact -> FAIL naming move.go), so nothing is broken now; the guard is simply one cwd away from being decorative.
issues.proposed_solution: AGENT-FIXABLE, two small edits in cli/internal/tui/plans_tab_test.go. (1) Add the reachability guard the precedent has: count the non-test `.go` files scanned and whether `model.go` was among them, then `t.Fatal("scanned N non-test .go files in the tui package (model.go seen: %v) - wrong cwd? this guard is vacuous unless it reads the package source")` when the count is 0 or model.go was never seen. (2) Replace the raw `os.Chdir(commaDir)` / `wd` / `t.Cleanup(func(){ os.Chdir(wd) })` / trailing `os.Chdir(wd)` dance in `TestAttachmentNormalize` with `t.Chdir(commaDir)` (Go 1.25), so the restore is guaranteed by the framework and the process cwd can never leak into a later test.
issues.fix_summary: TestNewFormIsTheOnlyFormConstructionSite now fails on an empty scan (scanned==0 or model.go unseen -> t.Fatalf, the skills_lint_test precedent); TestAttachmentNormalize's cwd mutation switched to Go 1.25 t.Chdir (self-restoring).
